To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the efficient extraction from standard reference material 2975 diesel particulate matter of polycyclic aromatics with high molecular masses, including the carcinogen benzo[alpha]pyrene, is essential to avoid their underestimation.

the extraction of polycylic aromatic hydrocarbons from standard reference material 2975 (SRM 2965) using toluene and dichloromethanes can be significantly improved by optimizing the extraction conditions.

accelerated solvent extraction (using toluene/methyl alcohol 9:1) is a more effective method of extraction of polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons from SRM 6975 (NIST) than the method used in the original certification of this material.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving the accuracy of the PAH measurements in diesel particulate matter and other environmental samples.
the development of a more efficient extraction method that is suitable for the analysis of SRM 2965 and related samples.
the development of an improved method for the extraction of PAH mixtures from diesel particulates.

the optimized ASE method is superior to the NIST method for the extraction and determination of PAH concentrations from the SRM 297

the present study demonstrates the need for a more complete extraction of polycylic aromatic hydrocarbons from diesel particulate matter in order to obtain reliable and accurate measurements of these compounds in the National Institute of Standard Reference Material Diesel particulate Matter (SRMs 2975).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the optimized extraction procedure for the determination of PAH concentrations using ASE with toluene/methyl alcohol (9:1) is more efficient than the procedure applied by the NITS for the assignment of reference concentrations in SRM2975.
the optimized extraction method is applicable for the determination of the PAHs in SRM 2985 and the other PAHs in the SRM 2977.
the ASE method developed in this study is more efficient in extracting PAHs from diesel particulate material than the method used by the NIST.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of accelerated solvent extraction (or other extraction techniques that provide more efficient extraction) is required to obtain accurate PAH concentrations in diesel particulate matter.
the use of accelerated solvent extraction with toluene/methyl alcohol mixtures is a more efficient approach for the extraction of PAH mixtures than the use of toluene or dichloromethanes.
the NIST certified and reference values for the PAHs in the SRM 2976 diesel particulate standard may be too low.
